/-!
# Hardy–Littlewood zeta function conjectures

Two conjectures of Hardy and Littlewood on the zeros of odd order of the function
$\zeta\bigl(\tfrac12 + it\bigr)$ on short intervals $(T, T + H]$ of the critical line, where
$T > 0$ is large and $H = T^{a + \varepsilon}$ with $\varepsilon > 0$ arbitrarily small.
Let $N_0(T)$ be the number of zeros of odd order of $\zeta\bigl(\tfrac12 + it\bigr)$ with
$t \in (0, T]$.

1. For any $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $T_0 = T_0(\varepsilon) > 0$ such that for
   $T \ge T_0$ and $H = T^{0.25 + \varepsilon}$ the interval $(T, T + H]$ contains a zero of
   odd order of the function $\zeta\bigl(\tfrac12 + it\bigr)$.
2. For any $\varepsilon > 0$ there exist $T_0 = T_0(\varepsilon) > 0$ and
   $c = c(\varepsilon) > 0$ such that for $T \ge T_0$ and $H = T^{0.5 + \varepsilon}$ the
   inequality $N_0(T + H) - N_0(T) \ge cH$ is true.

The first conjecture is open. The second was proved by Selberg (1942), who obtained the stronger
bound $N_0(T + H) - N_0(T) \ge cH \log T$ for $H = T^{0.5 + \varepsilon}$; Karatsuba (1984)
proved the same bound for $H = T^{27/82 + \varepsilon}$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Hardy–Littlewood zeta function conjectures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardy%E2%80%93Littlewood_zeta_function_conjectures)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- G. H. Hardy, J. E. Littlewood, *The zeros of Riemann's zeta-function on the critical line*,
  Math. Z. 10 (1921), 283–317. [doi:10.1007/bf01211614](https://doi.org/10.1007/bf01211614)
- A. Selberg, *On the zeros of Riemann's zeta-function*, Skr. Norske Vid. Akad. Oslo I (1942),
  no. 10, 1–59.
- A. A. Karatsuba, *On the zeros of the function ζ(s) on short intervals of the critical line*,
  Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR Ser. Mat. 48 (1984), no. 3, 569–584.
-/

def IsOddOrderZero (t : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Odd (analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta (1 / 2 + t * I))
blocks.docstring:
A real number $t$ is a *zero of odd order* of $\zeta\bigl(\tfrac12 + it\bigr)$ if the order
of vanishing of the Riemann zeta function at the point $\tfrac12 + it$ is odd.

The Riemann zeta function is analytic and not identically zero near every point
$\tfrac12 + it$, so `analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta (1 / 2 + t * I)` is the genuine multiplicity
of the zero $\tfrac12 + it$ of $\zeta$ (and is `0` when $\zeta(\tfrac12 + it) \ne 0$). Since the
substitution $s = \tfrac12 + it$ is affine, this is the same as the order of $t$ as a zero of the
function $t \mapsto \zeta\bigl(\tfrac12 + it\bigr)$ of a real variable.

justification.closest_existing_considered: analyticOrderAt / analyticOrderNatAt (Mathlib.Analysis.Analytic.Order), meromorphicOrderAt (Mathlib.Analysis.Meromorphic.Order); the ℕ-valued analyticOrderNatAt was used directly inside the definition (Odd on ℕ∞ would make Odd ⊤ true, so the ℕ version is safer).

@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem analyticAt_riemannZeta_critical_line (t : ℝ) :
    AnalyticAt ℂ riemannZeta (1 / 2 + t * I) := by
  have h : (1 / 2 + t * I : ℂ) ≠ 1 := fun h => by
    have := congrArg Complex.re h
    norm_num at this
  exact DifferentiableOn.analyticAt (s := {1}ᶜ)
    (fun z hz => (differentiableAt_riemannZeta hz).differentiableWithinAt)
    (isOpen_compl_singleton.mem_nhds h)
blocks.docstring:
The Riemann zeta function is analytic at every point $\tfrac12 + it$ of the critical line,
so the order of vanishing used in `IsOddOrderZero` is the genuine multiplicity, not a junk
value.

items: 'Zero of odd order of the function ζ(1/2+it)' is modeled as Odd (analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta (1/2 + t*I)), i.e. the multiplicity of s = 1/2+it as a zero of the complex function ζ is odd. This coincides with the order of t as a zero of the real-variable function t ↦ ζ(1/2+it), since the two differ by composition with the affine map t ↦ 1/2 + it (ζ(1/2+it) = (i(t−t₀))ⁿ g(1/2+it)). An odd order forces the order to be ≥ 1, so ζ(1/2+it) = 0 is implied (proved as the API lemma IsOddOrderZero.riemannZeta_eq_zero).

analyticOrderNatAt returns junk 0 when the function is not analytic or vanishes identically nearby; neither happens here: ζ is analytic at every 1/2+it (proved as API lemma analyticAt_riemannZeta_critical_line, since 1/2+it ≠ 1) and ζ is not identically zero near any point. Both junk cases would give order 0, which is not odd, so they could not create spurious odd-order zeros anyway.

N₀(T) is defined as Set.ncard of {t ∈ Set.Ioc 0 T | IsOddOrderZero t}; this set is finite (zeros of ζ are isolated and the segment is compact), so ncard is the genuine count. The article's N₀ counts odd-order zeros on the critical line in (0, T], not the usual N(T) of all zeros in the critical strip.

H = T^{0.25+ε} and H = T^{0.5+ε} are written as T ^ (1 / 4 + ε) and T ^ (1 / 2 + ε) with ε : ℝ, so these are real rpow with real exponents 0.25+ε and 0.5+ε (verified via pp.numericTypes). T > 0 is guaranteed by T ≥ T₀ > 0.

In part (ii) the inequality N₀(T+H) − N₀(T) ≥ cH is stated with both counts cast to ℝ, so that the subtraction is real subtraction, not truncated ℕ subtraction (mathematically equivalent since N₀ is monotone, but unambiguous).

Category: part (i) is research open; part (ii) is tagged research solved (not research open as the list-page status says) because Selberg (1942) proved the stronger bound N₀(T+H) − N₀(T) ≥ cH log T for H = T^{0.5+ε}, as stated in the article's Status section and in the decomposition-table notes. A reviewer who wants strict conformity to the list-page status should change this single tag. No formal_proof attribute is attached since no formal proof exists.
Only Wikipedia-style ASCII '1 / 2' is used for the point on the critical line: (1 / 2 + t * I : ℂ), verified to elaborate as complex 1/2 rather than a natural-number division.

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates formalized both slots with the same mathematics; no omissions to weigh. Points for a human reviewer: (1) Category of part (ii): the Wikipedia list marks the entry open (because part (i) is open), but part (ii) is settled (Selberg 1942 / Karatsuba 1984), so it is tagged `research solved` without a formal_proof attribute, consistent with repo practice; change to `research open` if strict conformity to the list entry is preferred. Note the article's Status section phrases Selberg's theorem with N(T) (all real zeros) rather than N₀, but Selberg's method and Karatsuba's statement give it for odd-order zeros. (2) 'Zero of odd order of ζ(1/2+it)' is modelled as odd multiplicity of the complex function riemannZeta at 1/2+it via analyticOrderNatAt (ℕ-valued; ⊤ and non-analytic junk map to 0, which is even). Using Odd on analyticOrderAt : ℕ∞ directly would be wrong since Odd ⊤ holds in ℕ∞ — all candidates avoided this. (3) N₀ uses Set.ncard, which returns 0 for infinite sets; the set is always finite (isolated zeros on a compact segment), so this is not a defect. (4) Exponents 0.25 and 0.5 are written 1/4 and 1/2 and verified to elaborate as real literals with Real.rpow.
